llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed UnifAPI connector wrapper with broad but expected external data access; the main caution is broad invocation wording and some unclear write labels.

dimensions.detail: The artifact coherently describes operating UnifAPI through OOMOL's oo CLI, including broad read and possible state-changing connector actions across social, SEO, web rendering, and research services.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The allowed command surface is scoped to Bash(oo *), and the skill tells agents to fetch live schemas before running actions, but the trigger text says to use it for any UnifAPI request and several read-described actions are tagged [write].
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: First-time setup includes a curl-to-bash or PowerShell installer and oo auth login, but these are disclosed fallback steps only after command/auth failures, not automatic startup behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The package contains only SKILL.md, no executable scripts, and its runtime authority is limited to the purpose-aligned oo connector commands.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: It relies on an installed CLI and an OOMOL-connected account with server-side credentials; no hidden local credential harvesting, background worker, or persistence mechanism is present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let the agent operate UnifAPI through your OOMOL account. Review requested actions and payloads carefully, especially anything tagged [write], and be aware that first-time setup may install the oo CLI and connect your UnifAPI credentials through OOMOL.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] expected: The flagged [write] labels are artifact-supported because multiple get/list actions are described as reads while tagged [write]; this is a documentation and consent-clarity issue, but it appears conservative rather than evidence of hidden mutation or exfiltration.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad 'ANY UnifAPI request' routing language is present and expands when the skill may be selected, but it remains bounded to UnifAPI and the oo CLI command surface.
